mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Y-o-y GDPC1 growth accelerates by > 2pp but SPX 60-day forward returns are negative > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM Manufacturing Index (proxied by INDPRO) falls below 45, indicating a contraction in manufacturing activity, it signals an impending recession that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 45 but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive > 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a 3-month period signals a rapidly weakening labor market, which will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending slows.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4% but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive > 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both decline by more than 5% year-over-year, it signals a broad-based weakening of consumer demand that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 5% y-o-y but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the ISM Manufacturing Index (proxied by INDPRO) is above 55 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals a tight labor market and strong industrial demand that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 55 and UNRATE < 4% but SPX 20-day forward returns are negative > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 3% year-over-year and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals a high-inflation environment that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the Fed tightens policy.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3% y-o-y and FEDFUNDS > 2% but SPX 60-day forward returns are positive > 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is growing by more than 200,000 jobs per month, it signals a very tight labor market that will drive wage inflation and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face higher costs.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS growth > 200k/month but SPX 20-day forward returns are positive > 60% of the time.
